hero.description: I am a statistician and data scientist from Côte d'Ivoire. For {years} years I have built the statistics, databases and models used by a trade finance bank, UN agencies, research institutes and an intergovernmental commodity body. These days my work is data architecture and AI systems in development finance. Before that I spent {iccoYears} years at the International Cocoa Organization as its statistician and econometrician, forecasting the cocoa market. I trained as a statistical engineer at ENSEA in Abidjan, hold a Master's in statistics and econometrics from Toulouse, and have MIT certificates in data engineering and applied AI. In June 2026 I submitted a DBA thesis on how development institutions adopt AI.

about.title: About
about.subtitle: Statistician and data scientist, from Côte d'Ivoire
about.bio:
I am a statistician and data scientist from Côte d'Ivoire. I trained at ENSEA in Abidjan and qualified as a statistics and information systems engineer in 2012. In 2017 I completed a Master's in statistics and econometrics at Université Toulouse I Capitole.

Since September 2023 I have been in Cairo at the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), where I look after data architecture and AI work: the Databricks lakehouse, data quality and master data, the pipelines that bring core banking and treasury data into the warehouse, and generative AI tools for internal use. From 2017 to 2023 I was the statistician and econometrician of the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) in Abidjan. I built its forecasting models and the statistical database behind its market reports.

Earlier, and sometimes in parallel, I ran data and monitoring and evaluation work for PAC-CI, ICRAF, FHI360, Barry-Callebaut and UNHCR in Abidjan, gave a training for ICRISAT in Mali, and worked remotely for IOM, UNIDIR and ITU.

I also hold certificates from MIT, Johns Hopkins University and the Corporate Finance Institute. In June 2026 I submitted my DBA thesis, Renting Intelligence, at the IIBM Institute of Business Management. It asks how the way development institutions source AI affects their performance.
